answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed when its behaviour diverges from its attested history: one thread of verifiable work, not a pile of cheap accounts. An attacker could still spin up a nebula of sock-puppet agents, but each one must lock real value and build reputation over time, so a flood costs as much as the honest network it tries to mimic. A lone zephyr of fake accounts blows through nothing: without stake and history, peers simply refuse to attest or trade with them.
